Fordlandia - the self-contained village and rubber plantation Henry Ford built in the Brazilian rain forest. c. 1935

Fordlândia is a now-abandoned, industrial town established in the Amazon Rainforest in 1928 by American industrialist Henry Ford to secure a source of cultivated rubber for the automobile manufacturing operations of the Ford Motor Company in the United States. Ford negotiated a deal with the Brazilian government granting him a concession of 10,000 km2 (3,900 sq mi) of land on the banks of the Rio Tapajós near the city of Santarém, Brazil, in exchange for a 9% interest in the profits generated. The project was ultimately a total failure.

Unfortunately, Henry made certain that the well-paid Brazilian workers ate an American diet, spoke English, and did not smoke or drink, as he had done with most all of his other workers. In this case it backfired and the workers in time rebelled and rioted. One other big mistake was the rubber trees that thrived in Asia did not grow well in the hilly, rocky and infertile land.
